item.title: Comprehensive DevOps Engineer Roadmap: Tools, Languages, and Learning Path
item.description:
Comprehensive DevOps Engineer Roadmap: Tools, Languages, and Learning Path

A step‑by‑step DevOps engineer roadmap has been published to help newcomers navigate the vast DevOps landscape.

🗺️ Overview

  • The roadmap provides a complete DevOps learning guide and aims to give you an idea about the landscape.
  • It is designed to guide you when you are confused about what to learn next, rather than pushing hype or trendy topics.
  • The roadmap encourages understanding why one tool may be better suited for a case than another.

⚙️ Core Version‑Control Tool: Git

  • All resources (files) are held in a GIT repository.
  • Files include both application code and infrastructure‑as‑code.
  • Git is a free source‑code‑management tool that tracks changes and enables multiple developers to work together on non‑linear development.
  • Popular Git platforms mentioned are GitLab and GitHub.
  • Essential Git commands to learn: git clone, branch, merge, and collaborating with pull‑requests.

🖥️ Programming Foundations

  • As a DevOps engineer, you should know at least one programming language for automation scripts.
  • Popular languages for DevOps include Python, Go, and JavaScript.
  • Python details:
    • Multi‑paradigm language.
    • Interpreted: code executes immediately after writing.
    • Syntax permits writing code in various styles.
    • Frequently recommended as the first language for new coders because of readability, consistency, and ease of use.
  • Fundamental programming concepts to master: syntax, if/else, loops, data structures, etc.

🖥️ Operating System Basics

  • An operating system acts as a bridge between a computer’s user and its hardware.
  • Its function is to provide a setting where users can conveniently and effectively run programs.

📚 Learning Resources & Community

  • The roadmap includes links to relevant learning resources.
  • If you want to learn more about DevOps, you are encouraged to subscribe to the author’s newsletter.
  • Users can star the project if they find it helpful for learning or starting a solution.
  • Support options: consider supporting the author on Patreon or download the PDF version of the roadmap.

🚀 Next Steps

  • Follow the roadmap to plan your DevOps education path.
  • Start by setting up a Git repository, learning basic Git commands, and choosing a programming language (Python is a strong first choice).
  • Continue building knowledge of OS concepts and infrastructure‑as‑code tools as you progress.

#devops #git #python #programming #roadmap

Source: milanm/DevOps-Roadmap

item.title: Bridgecrew launches Checkov for IaC and Open‑Source Package Security Scanning
item.description:
Bridgecrew launches Checkov for IaC and Open‑Source Package Security Scanning

Bridgecrew introduced Checkov, a static code analysis tool for infrastructure‑as‑code (IaC) that also performs software composition analysis (SCA) on container images and open‑source packages, helping developers prevent cloud misconfigurations and discover vulnerabilities early in the build process.

🔍 Overview

  • Checkov scans cloud infrastructure provisioned with Terraform, Terraform plan, CloudFormation, AWS SAM, Kubernetes, Helm charts, Kustomize, Dockerfile, Serverless, Bicep, OpenAPI, ARM Templates, or OpenTofu.
  • It also scans open‑source packages and images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs).
  • The tool powers Prisma Cloud Application Security, the developer‑first platform that codifies and streamlines cloud security throughout the development lifecycle.

🧩 How it works

  • Uses graph‑based scanning to provide context‑awareness policies.
  • Supports Python format for attribute policies and YAML format for both attribute and composite policies.
  • Detects AWS credentials in EC2 Userdata, Lambda environment variables, and Terraform providers.
  • Identifies secrets using regular expressions, keywords, and entropy‑based detection.

⚙️ Supported platforms

Category Supported Types
IaC templates Terraform, Terraform plan, Terraform JSON, CloudFormation, AWS SAM, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Dockerfile, Serverless framework, Ansible, Bicep, ARM, OpenTofu
CI pipelines Argo Workflows, Azure Pipelines, BitBucket Pipelines, Circle CI Pipelines, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI workflow files

📋 Key Features

  • Over 1 000 built‑in policies covering security and compliance best practices for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
  • Scans both IaC files and CI workflow definitions.
  • Performs Software Composition Analysis (SCA) for images and open‑source packages.
  • Provides context‑aware, graph‑based detection.
  • Enables policy authoring in Python and YAML.

🔐 Detection capabilities

  • Finds misconfigurations in IaC and cloud resources.
  • Detects AWS credentials in various locations.
  • Identifies secrets using regex, keywords, and entropy detection.
  • Scans container images and open‑source packages for CVEs.

🚀 Availability

  • Checkov is integrated into Prisma Cloud Application Security, delivering continuous security for cloud resources and IaC throughout the development lifecycle.

#Checkov #IaC #SCA #CloudSecurity

item.title: Encore expands platform for building production systems with real infrastructure
item.description:
Encore expands platform for building production systems with real infrastructure

Encore released an update that adds new capabilities for building, testing, and deploying production‑grade systems using real infrastructure throughout the development lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

Encore is the infrastructure platform for the intelligence era, where engineers and AI agents build production systems without waiting on infrastructure.

🧩 How It Works

  • Run and validate with real infrastructure locally and in preview environments, then deploy to your own AWS or GCP account.
  • Declare the resources your app needs (databases, Pub/Sub, object storage, caches, cron jobs, secrets) directly in your code, and encore run starts the whole system locally with real Postgres, real Pub/Sub semantics, and distributed tracing.
  • Each declaration becomes a node in Encore’s application graph.
  • Encore runs the migrations and stands up local equivalents on encore run, and provisions the cloud equivalents on deploy.
  • When you push a change that adds or modifies a resource, Encore diffs the application graph against the environment, provisions whatever is missing in your AWS or GCP account, and rolls out the new code against it.
  • Encore separates application semantics from environment-specific configuration.
  • In code, you define what resources your app needs, not how each environment should configure them.
  • That keeps services portable across clouds, regions, accounts, scale profiles, and local development.
  • Encore provisions every resource with sane production defaults, then helps you manage configuration separately from your application code.

⚙️ Key Features

  • Encore platform dashboard: easy to use knobs for all common settings like process allocation, instance sizes, replicas, etc.
  • Your AWS or GCP console: tweak anything directly in your cloud provider console.
  • Encore picks up the changes on the next deploy.
  • IaC: manage config for Encore‑provisioned resources alongside the rest of your infrastructure via the Terraform provider.
  • The same infrastructure model runs locally, in per‑PR preview environments, and in production.
  • Local: encore run starts the whole system locally: real Postgres, real Pub/Sub semantics, type‑safe service‑to‑service calls, plus a local dashboard with distributed tracing.
  • Infrastructure namespaces let multiple branches or agents work in parallel with isolated state.
  • Open a pull request and Encore sets up an ephemeral environment and (optionally) branches databases from a seed environment.
  • This Lets you do end‑to‑end validation against before merging to a shared staging environment.
  • Production: Push to deploy.
  • Encore diffs the application graph against the environment, provisions what is missing in your AWS or GCP account, wires up least‑privilege IAM based on the application’s code paths, and rolls out the new code.

🚀 Availability

The update is available to users who already have Encore set up on AWS or GCP and can be accessed through the standard encore run and deployment commands.

💡 Why It Matters

By letting developers define what resources are needed rather than how each environment configures them, Encore makes services portable across clouds, regions, and accounts while keeping configuration separate from application code. This reduces waiting time for infrastructure, enables safe end‑to‑end validation in preview environments, and enforces least‑privilege permissions automatically.
